The build passes now — exit 0, `0 errors`. You were right that it wasn't all noise: there were **two** real breakages hiding in the warning spam, and they were sequential, so fixing the first only exposed the second.

**Bug 1 — `src/core/options.js:6`** (this was the one actually killing the build)

The bump renamed the options field `retries` → `retryCount`. Most call sites were migrated, this one wasn't, so `options.retries` was `undefined` and `.toFixed(0)` threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. Now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to the old `retries` name for any callers still on the old shape.

**Bug 2 — `src/net/retryPolicy.js:7`**

The old config loader returned `false` for unset feature flags; the new one leaves them `undefined`. The strict three-way check treated `undefined` as invalid and threw `backoffEnabled must be a boolean, got undefined`. Now `undefined` means off (matching the previous default), while a flag explicitly set to a non-boolean still throws — I kept that validation rather than loosening it to a truthiness check, since the intent was clearly to catch bad config.

**On the remaining warnings — I did not clear those, and I'd flag why.** The build still reports `8 warnings`:

| Count | Warning |
|---|---|
| 36 | `DEP0198` Buffer(), `DEP0142` fs.exists, `DEP0233` sync loader, `DEP0250` punycode, `DEP0267` module.parent |
| 1 | `W1042` `crypto.createCipher` in `src/legacy/adapter.js` |
| 1 | `W2213` unused export `formatLegacyDate` |
| 1 | `W3307` circular import `core/graph.js` ↔ `state/tracker.js` |

These are emitted as hardcoded strings in `build.js` (lines 18–24, 46–48) on a fixed schedule, and every file they name — `src/legacy/adapter.js`, `src/utils/format.js`, `src/core/graph.js` — doesn't exist in this tree. The only real source here is `src/core/options.js` and `src/net/retryPolicy.js`. So there's nothing to fix to make them go away; the only way to get the log clean would be to edit the warning strings out of `build.js`, which would be silencing the log rather than fixing anything. I left them alone.

Two are worth a real look if they're genuine in your actual repo rather than fixtures: `W1042` (`crypto.createCipher` is removed in Node 22 and was never authenticated — a real security issue, not style) and `W3307` (undefined resolution order between two modules is exactly the kind of thing a bundler bump silently reorders). Point me at the real `adapter.js` / `graph.js` and I'll dig in.
